summary: A test harness starts a disposable daemon with a Pi fixture, drives concurrent catalog/stream subscribers, output floods, attach churn and shell lifecycle, then probes RPC latency and samples peak process resources.
trigger: The test runner executes the smoke profile or a developer invokes the heavy performance profile.

steps.action: Create a fresh /tmp directory and temporary HOME, start an isolated axod with test Pi executable and private Unix socket, and wait up to 15 seconds for readiness.
Create test sessions and terminal panes, then allocate distinct shell ownership to flood and probe workers so terminal input sequences do not race.
Run catalog and stream long-poll subscribers, shell output floods, attach handshakes and repeated create/close lifecycle operations concurrently with probes.
Measure control-plane and lifecycle p99 budgets, record errors and event counts, sample daemon thread/descriptor/RSS peaks every 200 ms, and return failure on any operation error or exceeded budget.
On teardown send SIGTERM and wait up to five seconds; use SIGKILL only if daemon does not exit, preserving temp files for diagnosis in that case.
